title: Inverse and implicit function theorems; submanifolds
summary: The inverse function theorem with its contraction-mapping proof; the implicit function theorem in Banach form; critical points and regular values; submanifolds and the regular-value theorem; the orthogonal group as a manifold; existence and uniqueness for ODEs via the inverse function theorem.

objectives.description: Prove the local inverse theorem by contraction, and derive the implicit theorem with the split-kernel hypothesis in Banach spaces.
Use a regular-value computation to identify a submanifold and its tangent spaces, including the orthogonal group.
Explain why local invertibility and local ODE existence do not assert global invertibility or existence.

preparation.description: Read lecture 4: Theorem 5.1 (inverse function theorem) and its contraction-mapping proof, Theorem 5.2 (implicit function theorem), Definition 5.3 (submanifold), Corollary 5.4.
Read lecture 5 §6: O(n) as the preimage of a regular value; the ODE existence argument. Compare with Hitchin's appendix §10.1.

commonMisconceptions.claim: A critical value cannot have a manifold as its inverse image.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Regularity is sufficient, not necessary. The zero level of the squared Euclidean norm is a single point, despite its zero derivative.

commonMisconceptions.claim: An everywhere invertible derivative makes a map globally invertible.
commonMisconceptions.correction: The inverse theorem is local; the exponential-polar map has an invertible derivative and periodic fibres.
